partner_context.their_ambition: Norway leads the world in marine electrification — over NOK 3.8 billion invested, dozens of battery-electric ferries already in service, and a national ambition to make its fjords the cleanest waterways on earth.
partner_context.their_pressure: From 1 January 2026 a zero-emission requirement takes effect in the UNESCO World Heritage fjords (Geirangerfjord and Nærøyfjord), with the broader fjord network following. The mandate turns clean propulsion from a nice-to-have into a license to operate — and the displacement ferries that remain are slow, leaving a faster, cleaner tier wide open.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier delivers vessels that are not just zero-emission but faster, smoother and silent over the protected fjord water — satisfying the mandate while transforming the visitor and commuter experience across the world's most scenic, most regulated waterways.

hero.eyebrow: Authority proposal · Kingdom of Norway · Fjord Ferry Network
hero.title: Navier × Fjord Norway — compliant, faster, silent
hero.subtitle: Foiling-electric vessels for the world's strongest zero-emission marine mandate.
hero.what_we_do_together: Navier brings a software-defined foiling-electric fleet that satisfies Norway's 2026 zero-emission fjord mandate while flying faster and quieter than the displacement ferries it replaces. The partnership pairs Navier's platform, captain training and certification path with the established Norwegian marine-electrification supply chain, charging norms and public acceptance — turning a regulatory forcing function into the best fjord experience on earth.

why_now: The 2026 zero-emission requirement in the UNESCO World Heritage fjords is the strongest pro-electric marine regulation anywhere. Norway has already built the supply chain, the charging norms and the public acceptance for electric vessels — what's missing is a tier that is clean and faster and silent. That is exactly Navier.
multimodal_fit: Navier slots into the existing express-boat and fjord-ferry network — Bergen's Strandkaiterminalen, the Geiranger and Flåm fjord heads, Stavanger's Ryfylke runs — taking the high-frequency commuter and sightseeing legs while conventional ferries keep heavy vehicle freight. Residents and visitors step from rail or coastal-express quay to foil to fjord village.

differentiation.why_navier: The only foiling-electric platform that satisfies Norway's zero-emission mandate while being faster and quieter than the ferries it replaces — software-defined, autonomy-ready, and supplied from a European factory base.

proof_points.claim: The regulatory tailwind is the strongest on earth.
proof_points.evidence: 2026 zero-emission requirement in the UNESCO World Heritage fjords, broader fjord network following.

proof_points.claim: The market is huge and boat-first.
proof_points.evidence: ~6M Fjord Norway visitors a year; sightseeing-by-boat is the core product.

proof_points.claim: The electrification supply chain already exists.
proof_points.evidence: NOK 3.8B+ invested, dozens of battery-electric ferries, ~29 routes electrifying.

proof_points.claim: The platform is proven in service.
proof_points.evidence: 10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out.

objections.concern: Can it handle deep, cold fjord water and long legs?
objections.response: The fjords are deep, sheltered and flat — ideal foiling conditions. Pioneer II covers the commuter and sightseeing legs all-electric; Quanta-LR hybrid carries the long Sognefjord and coastal-express line-hauls with no charging at small fjord-head villages.

Norway already runs electric ferries year-round; foiling adds a smoother, faster ride in the protected fjord waters, with routing and scheduling tuned to the season exactly as the existing fleet does.

objections.concern: Does it fit the existing ferry network?
objections.response: Yes — it slots into the express-boat and fjord-ferry terminals already in use (Strandkaiterminalen, fjord heads), taking high-frequency passenger legs while conventional ferries keep vehicle freight.

objections.concern: Can it be delivered against the 2026 mandate timeline?
objections.response: Phased: launch on the shorter mandate-critical UNESCO fjord legs first (where diesel is now banned), then scale to the commuter and coastal corridors.

phases.label: The World Heritage fjords, zero-emission
phases.narrative: The two UNESCO fjords where zero-emission operation is mandated from 2026 — Nærøyfjord (Flåm–Gudvangen) and Geirangerfjord (Geiranger–Hellesylt) — flown clear of the water: near-silent, zero-wake, and fully within the mandate on day one.

phases.label: The Sognefjord express and commuter crossings
phases.narrative: The fast express legs into the fjord network — Bergen to Balestrand and Flåm, and the Bergen–Askøy commuter crossing — where foiling speed and range finally retire diesel on the long runs.

phases.label: The long coastal fjords
phases.narrative: The longest fjord express — the Lysefjord line from Stavanger — a clean line-haul that keeps the remotest fjord communities fast, connected and zero-emission.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling-electric fleet, captain training, certification path and the operating playbook for protected-water foiling.
the_ask.partner_brings: Fjord terminal access, the route-by-route rollout sequence, the Norwegian marine-electrification supply chain and public-sector relationships.
the_ask.next_step: Launch the mandate-critical UNESCO fjord legs in 2026 and publish Norway as the global zero-emission marine reference.

close.title: The cleanest waterways on earth, flying.
close.body: Norway already mandated zero-emission fjords and built the supply chain to deliver them. Navier is the tier that makes compliant also mean faster, silent and unforgettable — the global reference for regulated clean marine mobility.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open water and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Three forces just converged: the technology crossed from prototype to platform (10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out), decarbonization mandates turned legacy diesel fleets into stranded liabilities, and the hybrid removed the 'no charging' excuse. The marine layer is being claimed cluster-by-cluster right now.

end_state.headline: A national foiling fjord network across the world's most regulated waterways.
end_state.addressable_footprint: Bergen, Geiranger, Stavanger and the wider Fjord Norway network — UNESCO World Heritage fjords, commuter island runs and the coastal express.

steady_state.platform_mix: Pioneer II for fjord & commuter legs; Quanta-LR for Sognefjord & coastal express
steady_state.the_opportunity: ~6M annual fjord visitors plus year-round commuter demand under a binding zero-emission mandate.

end_state.narrative: Steady state is a national foiling fjord layer: every UNESCO fjord, commuter island and coastal-express corridor served by fast, silent, zero-emission vessels — the global reference for regulated clean marine mobility.

levers: Anchor the proposal on the UNESCO World Heritage fjord legs where zero-emission is MANDATED from 2026 (Nærøyfjord: Flåm–Gudvangen; Geirangerfjord: Geiranger–Hellesylt), then extend to the Sognefjord express and commuter crossings, then the longer coastal express corridors. Foiling-electric wins on the fast express-boat legs where range/speed kept diesel longest. Domestic-first; no cross-border link.

Norway already runs the world's first battery-electric car ferry (MF Ampere, 2015) and hydrogen ferry (MF Hydra); a foiling-electric platform extends that leadership to the fast express-boat legs, where speed and range have kept diesel in service the longest — decarbonizing exactly the corridors the 2026 mandate targets.
